items.question: L, N and Z lie on a straight line. Rays NM and NY lie on the same side of that line, in the order NL, NM, NY, NZ. If angle LNM is g degrees and angle YNZ is h degrees, find angle MNY.
items.explanation: Adjacent angles on a straight line add to 180°. Here g + angle MNY + h = 180°, so angle MNY = 180°−g°−h°. Both given angles must be subtracted.
items.observed_question: In the diagram above angle LNM and angle YNZ are represented by g and h respectively. Find ∠MNY

diagram_evidence.relationships: L,N,Z collinear; upper-half rays NL,NM,NY,NZ; g=LNM; h=YNZ. No numeric angle invented.
diagram_evidence.public_prompt_adaptation: Needed figure relationships transcribed into self-contained verbal prompt; source scan not published.

per_option_reasoning.A: Subtract both adjacent given angles from the straight angle.
per_option_reasoning.B: Uses 360 degrees and adds h; inconsistent with the upper straight angle.
per_option_reasoning.C: Adds h after expanding its brackets; both adjacent angles must be subtracted.
per_option_reasoning.D: Uses a full turn rather than the straight angle LNZ.
